cognitive_validation.rationale: The hunting methods (smoothbore ballistics, tracking by kill remains, firing dry reeds with the wind) are coherent and nonsupernatural, but this concerns method, not a world-altering difference.

novum_candidates.description: A dangerous single-handed lion hunt in which Quatermain attacks a family of lions, using fire to flush them from a reed pan, and is ultimately maimed by the black-maned lion.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The visceral terror of lying paralyzed among feeding lions and the lasting maiming provide reader-facing intensity, but this is mundane physical danger rather than estrangement from an empirical norm.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The hunt drives the entire embedded narrative and its consequence (permanent lameness), but centrality within an ordinary adventure tale does not make it a novum absent the novelty dimension.

novelty.rationale: A lion hunt in 19th-century Africa is entirely within the authorial empirical norm. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical environment; it is an adventure-genre event, not a novum.

cognitive_validation.rationale: No systematic or immanent account of such a people is given; the text offers only rumour and hope, so its coherence cannot be assessed.

novum_candidates.description: The rumoured lost white people said to exist in the unexplored African interior, which Quatermain seeks in his final quest.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The remote Tana mission location and the vanishing into the interior gesture toward an unexplored beyond, but the lost people remain rumour and produce no developed storyworld consequence.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The rumoured white people appear only in the framing preface and do not govern the central embedded lion-hunt narrative; they are a peripheral device.

novelty.rationale: A hidden lost civilization is a potential world-altering difference typical of Haggard's romances, but in this text it exists only as unverified rumour in the frame; it is never realized or developed as an actual storyworld fact.
